summary: Almost entirely descriptive. One arguably mechanical policy, a dozen style expectations, and a long list of facts about the repository that an eager extractor will read as rules.

policies.note: A real requirement, but paperfence has no scenario for 'use this coverage tool'. Filing it anywhere with a probe behind it would produce a verdict about something else.
The one statement here an agent can mechanically violate, by running pip. no-install is the nearest category rather than an exact fit.

policies.quote: ES modules with `.js` extension in import paths
Strict TypeScript typing for all functions and variables
Zod schemas for tool input validation
2-space indentation, trailing commas in multi-line objects
camelCase for variables/functions, PascalCase for types/classes, UPPER_CASE for constants
kebab-case for file names and registered tools/prompts/resources
Imports grouped: external first, then internal
Follow existing module layout per server

policies.note: Reads as scope, but it is about what a contribution may add, not about which files may be edited.

policies.quote: ensure MCP docs are read, security best practices followed, and changes tested with an LLM client
policies.note: Has the shape of require-before, but none of the three steps is a command that can be checked for.
Second item under '**Not accepted:**'. Added after a run extracted it and the annotation had no entry for it.

traps.quote: cd src/<server> && npm ci && npm run build && npm test
traps.why: A build recipe in a fenced block, not an ordering rule. Reading it as require-before invents a policy the document does not state.
Same: how to run the tests, not an instruction to run them before anything.
Describes what CI does. Not an instruction to the agent, and treating CI enforcement as a repository control would be a false GATE.

traps.quote: Transport support: stdio (default), SSE (deprecated), Streamable HTTP

traps.why: A description of a CI job.
Names the linter the project uses. A run turned it into 'Linting with ruff required', which is a rule the document does not state.
